stances.claim: President Joseph Ejercito Estrada has asked CJP during their encounters: 'The Constitution states that the Vice President may become President only in case of death, permanent disability, removal from office, or resignation of the President. Why then was I ousted, and GMA installed as President when, clearly, I have not died, have no permanent disability, have not been removed from office, and have not resigned?' He also lamented: 'During my two and half years in office, I named several justices. Why is it that none of them dissented from the 13-0 decision ousting me? Why did CJ Davide, whom I also appointed, swear in GMA as permanent President, not merely as Acting President?'

The Supreme Court's role in Edsa II began on the early morning of Saturday, Jan 20 2001. The massive chanting throng at the Edsa Shrine was poised to march on and take over Malacañang. The AFP and PNP majors had publicly withdrawn support from Estrada and pledged allegiance to GMA; majority of the Cabinet had resigned. Estrada could no longer govern, but GMA had no legal authority either -- no effectively functioning government. Worried about violence, civil strife, and bloodshed, CJP proposed that Arroyo be sworn in as 'Acting President.' CJ Davide agreed, and in a hurriedly-convened session the justices concurred. But at the historic noon oath-taking at Edsa Shrine, Davide swore GMA in 'to act as President,' not as 'Acting President.'

The following Monday, Jan 22, some justices were furious at the different oath administered. Davide accepted full responsibility, saying 'to act as President' were neutral words and could, at the proper time and case and after full hearing, be clarified. After lengthy deliberation, the Court unanimously passed a resolution to confirm the CJ's authority to swear in GMA as 'President of the Philippines.' In Estrada v. Desierto (March 2 2001) came the proper time and case -- the Court voted 13-0 (Davide and CJP inhibited on motion of Estrada's counsel Rene A.V. Saguisag) upholding the ouster and legitimacy of GMA's presidency.

The decision (written by J. Puno, concurred in by Melo + Quisumbing + Gonzaga-Reyes + de Leon + Buena 'in the result') explained that resignation may be express or implied. Though Estrada had not written any express resignation, 'the totality of prior, contemporaneous and posterior facts and circumstantial evidence,' put together, could be and were construed as implied resignation -- hence the term 'constructive resignation.' The Edgardo Angara diary (Inquirer serialized) provided 'an authoritative window' on Estrada's 'intent to resign,' confirmed by his leaving Malacañang without disability-claim. Constructive resignation was strengthened by Congress confirming Guingona's nomination as VP to replace GMA, and Congress clearly rejecting Estrada's claim of being merely a 'President on leave.'
stances.rhetorical_move: constructive-resignation doctrinal-coinage + totality-test + three-pillar evidence framing

stances.claim: Concurring-opinion variety: J. Bellosillo opined that Estrada suffered from permanent 'functional' disability; J. Mendoza clarified that what enabled GMA 'to assume the presidency was... the vacuum in executive leadership which made the government rife for seizure by lawless elements'; J. Vitug held that Estrada practically abandoned the presidency, an act equivalent to resignation. Dissenters Kapunan + Pardo + Ynares-Santiago + Sandoval-Gutierrez ruled Estrada had not resigned. But the stark reality was that GMA had actually taken over and was recognized as such by Congress, the international community, and the Filipino people. In Gutierrez's words, 'this Court has to declare as a fact what in fact exists.' Pardo, Santiago, and Gutierrez were Estrada appointees -- their 'reality' stance answers Estrada's earlier question.

Though Estrada still maintains he did not resign, CJP thinks he has accepted the immutability of his fall -- all he now hopes and prays for is to redeem himself in the way he knows best: by serving the people for one last time as mayor of Manila. With full knowledge of his checkered past and his heroic effort to resurrect from misfortune, the people have spoken loud and clear. And in a democracy, the ultimate axiom is: Vox populi, vox Dei.

notable_anecdotes: CJP-personal-encounters-with-Estrada framing -- 'asked President Joseph Ejercito Estrada during our encounters' -- among CJP's most autobiographically-grounded column-premises, signaling a former-justice-now-columnist relationship with the man he helped depose.

Estrada's two-rhetorical-questions verbatim -- Constitution-VP-succession-requirements (death/permanent-disability/removal/resignation -- Estrada satisfied none) + 'Why is it that none of [my-appointed justices] dissented from the 13-0 decision ousting me? Why did CJ Davide, whom I also appointed, swear in GMA as permanent President, not merely as Acting President?' -- captured with full quotation marks as Estrada's own words.

CJP-as-Acting-President-proposer disclosure -- 'Worried that violence, civil strife and bloodshed would ensue, I proposed that Arroyo be sworn in as Acting President' -- a rare candid disclosure that CJP originated the institutional-cushion proposal that ultimately resolved the Edsa II vacuum.

The to-act-as-President-vs-Acting-President distinction -- CJP's wry observation that Davide actually swore GMA in 'to act as President' (not 'Acting President') at the Edsa Shrine noon oath-taking -- a subtle wording-shift that infuriated 'some justices' the following Monday but was later normalized by unanimous resolution confirming Davide's authority.

The Saguisag-motion-for-CJP-inhibition fact -- that Estrada's counsel Rene A.V. Saguisag moved for CJP's inhibition (along with Davide) in Estrada v. Desierto, explaining why CJP did not vote in the 13-0 decision -- a procedural-bio-detail that contextualizes the column's stance.

The Edgardo Angara diary Inquirer-serialization 'authoritative window' citation -- using a serialized executive-secretary memoir as constructive-resignation evidence is a striking evidentiary move now embedded in the doctrine.

The constructive-resignation doctrinal-coinage itself -- 'the totality of prior, contemporaneous and posterior facts and circumstantial evidence... could be and were in fact construed as implied resignation' -- a doctrinal formulation that has since shaped PH constitutional law on presidential succession.

The Pardo + Santiago + Gutierrez Estrada-appointee-but-reality-stance detail -- 'Pardo, Santiago and Gutierrez were Estrada appointees. Their reality stance answers Estrada's earlier question' -- directly addressing why even his own appointees did not dissent in their concurrence, via Gutierrez's verbatim 'this Court has to declare as a fact what in fact exists.'
The closing 'Vox populi, vox Dei' Latin-axiom -- democracy-as-ultimate-axiom framing for the 2013 mayoral race as Estrada's redemption-by-popular-vote.

The 'last time as mayor of Manila' redemption-framing -- capturing the moment in 2013 (just before Estrada won the Manila mayoralty later that year) when CJP offered a pre-emptive sympathy-but-firm-on-doctrine reading of his rival's bid.

Why is it that none of them dissented from the 13-0 decision ousting me? Why did Chief Justice [Hilario] Davide, whom I also appointed, swear in GMA as permanent President, not merely as Acting President?' CJP focuses on his conversations with Estrada. The Supreme Court's role in Edsa II began the early morning of Saturday Jan 20 2001 -- the massive Edsa-Shrine throng was poised to march on Malacañang where Estrada and supporters were entrenched; the AFP and PNP majors had publicly withdrawn support and pledged allegiance to GMA; the majority of Cabinet had resigned.
